title: Kuru Fasulye
subtitle: Turkish white bean stew with tomato and pepper
excerpt: This is the everyday bean stew of Turkey, eaten from street canteens to home kitchens. Dried white beans are slow-cooked with tomato paste and sweet pepper until the sauce is thick and the beans are completely soft.
sourceNotes: Staple of Turkish home cooking and lokan ta restaurants. Traditionally made with dried haricot or cannellini beans soaked overnight.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well. Cool fully, then freeze in portions. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the quantity without any changes. Use a large pot and check the liquid level every 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew tastes better the next day. Make it up to two days ahead and reheat before serving.

content.text: Kuru fasulye is a Turkish bean stew built on slow-cooked cannellini beans and a rich tomato-pepper base. Soak the beans overnight so they cook evenly. The sauce should cling to the beans; if it is thin, keep the lid off for the last 15 minutes.

items.prepNote: dried, soaked in cold water overnight

content.text: Drain and rinse the soaked beans. Put them in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to the boil. Boil hard for 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in the same saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and red pepper and cook for 3 minutes more.
Stir in the tomato puree and paprikas. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens slightly.
Add the tinned tomatoes and 600 ml of water. Stir well. Add the par-boiled beans and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60 to 70 minutes. Stir every 20 minutes. The beans should be completely soft and easy to break with a spoon.
Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes if the sauce looks too thin. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with parsley. Serve with crusty bread or plain rice.

items.symptom: The beans are still firm after 70 minutes.
items.cause: They were not soaked long enough, or the water was too hard.
items.fix: Keep cooking and add more water. Old beans can take up to 2 hours. Adding salt too early can also slow softening, so season only at the end.

items.cause: Too much water was added, or the lid was kept on throughout.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes to reduce.

items.cause: Not enough salt, or the paprika was old and stale.
items.fix: Season firmly at the end. Use fresh paprika; it loses its punch quickly once opened.
